correctness.rationale: For prescribed k disjoint pairing edges, probability is 1/[(q−1)(q−3)…(q−2k+1)]. Internal two-stub choices give EL=S/(q−1). Ordered cross-pair pairings on four stubs between i,j contribute 2 a_i a_j, yielding EP=B/[(q−1)(q−3)]. A loop compatible with such a double edge must avoid the four occupied stubs; its count is S−(2d_i−3)−(2d_j−3), yielding ELP=(BS−T)/[(q−1)(q−3)(q−5)]. Subtracting moments gives the exact covariance. For d_i=r, substitute S=va, B=v(v−1)a², T=2v(v−1)a²(2r−3), factor the sign vr(2−r)+(2r−3); r=2 is positive and r≥3 negative. The q=4 (v,r)=(2,2) perfect matchings give −4/9 directly, while asymptotics follow by powers of v. Independent enumeration of all labeled pairings across 701 weak degree profiles q=6,8,10 checked exact rational EL, EP, ELP, and covariance (2804 assertions) and 167 regular sign cases; these bounded checks supplement unrestricted counting.

value.rationale: A finite-size positive/negative dependence reversal at the natural degree-two boundary is a mathematically meaningful correction to the heuristic that asymptotically independent defect counts should have no signed dependence. The all-profile closed formula and the different O(v^−2) versus O(v^−1) decay scales can inform finite configuration-model approximations and are not merely restating Poisson limits.

final_claim: For uniformly paired labeled half-edges of any nonnegative degree profile with even total q≥6, Cov(loop count, parallel-edge-pair count)=[4BS−(q−1)T]/[(q−1)²(q−3)(q−5)] for the specified witness sums; regular degree two yields positive covariance for at least three vertices, whereas every regular degree at least three yields negative covariance, with the q=4 exception −4/9.
